plan: Jeremiah 39:11-18; Jeremiah 40:1-6; 2 Kings 25:8-21; Jeremiah 52:12-27; 2 Chronicles 36:15-21; Lamentations 1:1-22

readings.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Command
readings.subtitle: Jeremiah is entrusted to Gedaliah's care.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 39:11] And Neḇuḵaḏretstsar the sovereign of Baḇel gave a command concerning Yirmeyahu to Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, saying, [12] “Take him and look after him, and do no harm whatsoever to him, but do to him even as he shall speak to you.” [13] And Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, and Neḇushazban the Raḇsaris, Něrḡal-Shar’etser the Raḇmaḡ, and all the sovereign of Baḇel’s chief officers sent, [14] and had Yirmeyahu taken from the court of the guard, and gave him to Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, son of Shaphan, to take him home. And he dwelt among the people.

readings.title: A Promise to Ebed-Melech
readings.subtitle: His life will be spared for his trust in YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 39:15] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had come to Yirmeyahu while he was shut up in the court of the guard, saying, [16] “Go, and you shall speak to Eḇeḏ-Meleḵ the Kushite, saying, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> words upon this city for evil and not for good, and they shall be before you in that day.</dq> [17] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall deliver you in that day,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“so that you are not given into the hand of the men of whom you are afraid.</dq> [18] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> shall rescue you, and you shall not fall by the sword. But your life shall be as a prize to you, for you have put your trust in <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”

readings.title: Jeremiah Freed at Ramah
readings.subtitle: He chooses to dwell with the remnant under Gedaliah.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 40:1] The word that came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> after Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him bound in chains among all the exiles from Yerushalayim and Yehuḏah, who were being exiled to Baḇel. [2] And the chief of the guard took Yirmeyahu and said to him, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has spoken <dn>את</dn> this evil on this place. [3] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has brought it on, and has done, as <dn>He</dn> has said. Because you have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and did not obey <dn>His</dn> voice, therefore this matter has come upon you. [4] “And now, see, I loosen you today from the chains that were on your hand. If it seems good to you to come with me to Baḇel, come, and I shall look after you. But if it seems wrong for you to come with me to Baḇel, remain here. See, all the land is before you, go wherever it seems good and right for you to go.” [5] And before he replied, Neḇuzaraḏan said, “Or go back to Geḏalyah son of Aḥiqam, son of Shaphan, whom the sovereign of Baḇel has made governor over the cities of Yehuḏah, and dwell with him among the people, or go wherever it seems right for you to go.” And the chief of the guard gave him provisions and a gift and let him go. [6] So Yirmeyahu went to Geḏalyah son of Aḥiqam, to Mitspah, and dwelt with him among the people who were left in the land.

readings.title: The Burning of Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: Nebuzaradan destroys the temple, the palace, and the city walls.
readings.text: [2 Kings 25:8] And in the fifth new moon, on the seventh of the new moon, which was the nineteenth year of Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sovereign of Baḇel, Neḇuzaraḏan the chief of the guard, a servant of the sovereign of Baḇel, came to Yerushalayim. [9] And he burned <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the house of the sovereign, and <dn>את</dn> all the houses of Yerushalayim – even <dn>את</dn> every great house he burned with fire. [10] And all the army of the Kasdim who were with the chief of the guard broke down <dn>את</dn> the walls of Yerushalayim all around. [11] And Neḇuzaraḏan the chief of the guard took into exile <dn>את</dn> the rest of the people who were left in the city and the deserters who deserted to the sovereign of Baḇel, with the rest of the multitude. [12] But the chief of the guard left some of the poor of the land as vinedressers and farmers.

readings.title: The Plundering of the Temple
readings.subtitle: The bronze pillars, Sea, and utensils are carried to Babylon.
readings.text: [2 Kings 25:13] And <dn>את</dn> the bronze columns that were in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> the stands and <dn>את</dn> the bronze Sea that were in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the Kasdim broke in pieces, and took <dn>את</dn> their bronze away to Baḇel. [14] And they took <dn>את</dn> the pots, and <dn>את</dn> the shovels, and <dn>את</dn> the snuffers, and <dn>את</dn> the ladles, and <dn>את</dn> all the bronze utensils the priests used in the service. [15] And the chief of the guard took <dn>את</dn> the fire holders and <dn>את</dn> the basins which were of solid gold and solid silver. [16] The bronze of all these utensils was beyond measure – the two columns, the one Sea, and the stands, which Shelomoh had made for the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [17] The height of one column was eighteen cubits, and the capital on it was of bronze. And the height of the capital was three cubits, and the network and pomegranates all around the capital were all of bronze. And the second column was the same, with a network.

readings.title: Execution of the Leaders
readings.subtitle: The chief priests and officials are put to death at Riblah.
readings.text: [2 Kings 25:18] And the chief of the guard took <dn>את</dn> Serayah the chief priest, and <dn>את</dn> Tsephanyahu the second priest, and <dn>את</dn> the three doorkeepers. [19] And out of the city he took <dn>את</dn> a certain eunuch who was appointed over the men of battle, and <dn>את</dn> five men of those who saw the sovereign’s face, who were found in the city, and <dn>את</dn> the chief scribe of the army who mustered the people of the land, and <dn>את</dn> sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city. [20] And Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, took them and made them go to the sovereign of Baḇel at Riblah. [21] And the sovereign of Baḇel struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Ḥamath. So he exiled Yehuḏah from its own land.

readings.title: Nebuzaradan Destroys the City
readings.subtitle: The House of YeHoVaH and the great houses are burned.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 52:12] And on the tenth of the fifth new moon, which was the nineteenth year of sovereign Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel, Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, who served the sovereign of Baḇel, came to Yerushalayim, [13] and he burned <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> the sovereign’s house, and <dn>את</dn> all the houses of Yerushalayim, and <dn>את</dn> all the houses of the great men, he burned with fire. [14] And all the army of the Kasdim who were with the chief of the guard broke down <dn>את</dn> all the walls of Yerushalayim all around. [15] And Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, exiled <dn>את</dn> some of the poor people, and <dn>את</dn> the rest of the people who were left in the city, and the defectors who had gone over to the sovereign of Baḇel, and the rest of the craftsmen. [16] But Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, left some of the poor of the land as vinedressers and farmers.

readings.title: The Temple Spoils
readings.subtitle: The bronze, silver, and gold vessels are taken to Babylon.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 52:17] And the Kasdim broke <dn>את</dn> the bronze columns that were in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> the stands and <dn>את</dn> the bronze Sea that were in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and brought <dn>את</dn> all their bronze to Baḇel. [18] They also took away <dn>את</dn> the pots, and <dn>את</dn> the shovels, and <dn>את</dn> the snuffers, and <dn>את</dn> the bowls, and <dn>את</dn> the ladles, and <dn>את</dn> all the bronze utensils with which they served, [19] and <dn>את</dn> the basins, and <dn>את</dn> the fire holders, and <dn>את</dn> the bowls, and <dn>את</dn> the pots, and <dn>את</dn> the lampstands, and <dn>את</dn> the ladles, and <dn>את</dn> the cups, whatever was of solid gold and whatever was of solid silver, the chief of the guard took. [20] The two columns, one Sea, the twelve bronze bulls which were under it, and the stands, which Sovereign Shelomoh had made for the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weighing. [21] As for the columns, the height of one column was eighteen cubits, and its circumference was twelve cubits, and its thickness was four fingers, hollow. [22] And a capital of bronze was on it. And the height of one capital was five cubits, with a network and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. And the second column, with pomegranates was the same. [23] And there were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides. All the pomegranates on the network were one hundred, all around.

readings.title: Judah's Officials Executed
readings.subtitle: They are struck down by the king of Babylon in the land of Hamath.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 52:24] And the chief of the guard took <dn>את</dn> Serayah the chief priest, and <dn>את</dn> Tsephanyah the second priest, and <dn>את</dn> the three doorkeepers. [25] And from the city he took <dn>את</dn> one eunuch who was in charge of the men of battle, and <dn>את</dn> seven men who saw the sovereign’s face, who were found in the city, and <dn>את</dn> the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and <dn>את</dn> sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city. [26] And Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, took <dn>את</dn> these and brought them to the sovereign of Baḇel at Riḇlah, [27] and the sovereign of Baḇel struck them and put them to death at Riḇlah in the land of Ḥamath. Thus Yehuḏah was exiled from its own land.

readings.title: The Reason for Exile
readings.subtitle: Mocking God's messengers until there was no remedy.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 36:15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers sent to them, by <dn>His</dn> messengers, rising up early and sending them, for <dn>He</dn> had compassion on <dn>His</dn> people and on <dn>His</dn> dwelling place. [16] But they were mocking the messengers of <dn>Elohim</dn> and despising <dn>His</dn> words and scoffing at <dn>His</dn> prophets, until the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> arose against <dn>His</dn> people, until there was no healing. [17] Therefore <dn>He</dn> brought against them the sovereign of the Kasdim, and he killed their young men with the sword in the House of their set-apart place, and had no compassion on young man or maiden, on the aged or the weak – <dn>He</dn> gave all into his hand. [18] And <dn>את</dn> all the utensils from the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>, great and small, and <dn>את</dn> the treasures of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> the treasures of the sovereign and of his leaders, all these he brought to Baḇel. [19] And they burned <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and broke down <dn>את</dn> the wall of Yerushalayim, and burned <dn>את</dn> all its palaces with fire, and destroyed <dn>את</dn> all its valuable utensils. [20] And those who escaped from the sword he exiled to Baḇel, where they became servants to him and his sons until the reign of the reign of Persia, [21] in order to fill <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by the mouth of Yirmeyahu, until the land had enjoyed her Sabbaths. As long as she lay waste she kept Sabbath, until seventy years were completed.

readings.title: How Lonely Sits the City
readings.subtitle: Zion, once a princess, has become a slave without splendor.
readings.text: [Lamentations 1:1] How alone she sits, The city once great with people! Like a widow she has become, One great among the nations! A princess among provinces has become a slave! [2] She weeps bitterly at night, And her tears are upon her cheeks. Among all her lovers there is no comforter for her. All her friends have betrayed her, They have become her enemies. [3] Yehuḏah has gone into exile, Because of affliction and because of harsh labour. She has dwelt among nations, She has found no rest. All her pursuers have overtaken her Between narrow places. [4] The ways to Tsiyon mourn For no one comes to the appointed times. All her gates are deserted, Her priests sigh, her maidens are afflicted, And she has bitterness. [5] Her adversaries have become chief, Her enemies have become at ease. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has afflicted her Because of her many transgressions. Her children have gone into captivity before the enemy. [6] And all the splendour has departed From the daughter of Tsiyon. Her rulers have become like buck, They have found no pasture, And they go powerless before the pursuer.

readings.title: Remembrance of Sin
readings.subtitle: Jerusalem's defilement is seen by all; her people sigh for bread.
readings.text: [Lamentations 1:7] In the days of her affliction and wandering, Yerushalayim remembered all her precious matters She had in the days of old. When her people fell into the hand of the enemy, With no one to help her, The adversaries saw her, They mocked at her destruction. [8] Yerushalayim has sinned greatly, Therefore she has become defiled. All who esteemed her despised her Because they have seen her nakedness. She herself has sighed and turned away. [9] Her uncleanness is in her skirts. She did not keep in mind her latter end, And has gone down appallingly, There was no one to comfort her. “See, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, my affliction, For the enemy has made himself great!” [10] The adversary has spread his hand Over <dn>את</dn> all her precious matters; Indeed, she has seen: The nations have entered her set-apart place, Those whom You commanded not to enter Your assembly. [11] All her people are sighing, seeking bread. They have given <dn>את</dn> their precious matters For food, to bring back life. “See, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and look, For I have become despised.”

readings.title: A Cry of Unparalleled Pain
readings.subtitle: The city weeps for the affliction brought by YeHoVaH's burning displeasure.
readings.text: [Lamentations 1:12] “Is it naught to you, All you who pass by? Look and see if there is any pain like my pain, Which has been brought on me, Which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has inflicted on me In the day of <dn>His</dn> burning displeasure. [13] “From above <dn>He</dn> has sent fire into my bones, And it overpowered them; <dn>He</dn> has spread a net for my feet and turned me back; <dn>He</dn> has laid me waste and faint all the day. [14] “The yoke of my transgressions Has been bound by <dn>His</dn> hand, Woven together and thrust upon my neck. <dn>He</dn> has made my strength stumble, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given me into hands Which <dn>I</dn> am unable to withstand. [15] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has trodden down <dn>את</dn> all my strong men in my midst, <dn>He</dn> has called an appointed time Against me to crush my young men. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has trodden down as in a winepress <dn>את</dn> The maiden daughter of Yehuḏah. [16] “This is why <dn>I</dn> weep. My eye, my eye is running down with water, Because the comforter, Who could bring back my life, Has been far from me. My children are stunned, For the enemy has prevailed.”

readings.title: Confession and Plea
readings.subtitle: Zion acknowledges her rebellion and calls for justice upon her enemies.
readings.text: [Lamentations 1:17] Tsiyon spreads out her hands, There is no comforter for her. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded concerning Ya‛aqoḇ, <dn>His</dn> neighbours are his adversaries. Yerushalayim has become an uncleanness among them. [18] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is righteous, for <dn>I</dn> rebelled against <dn>His</dn> mouth. Hear now, all peoples, and see my pain. My maidens and my young men have gone into captivity. [19] <dn>I</dn> called for my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and my elders breathed their last in the city, While they sought food to bring back their life. [20] “See, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that <dn>I</dn> am in distress. My inward parts are boiling up, My heart is overturned within me, For <dn>I</dn> have been very rebellious. From without the sword has bereaved, At home it is like death. [21] “They have heard that <dn>I</dn> sighed, With no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my calamity, They have rejoiced that You have done it. You shall bring on <dn>את</dn> the day that You have announced, So let them become like me. [22] “Let <dn>את</dn> all their evil come before You, And do to them as You have done to me For all my transgressions. For my sighs are many, and my heart is faint.”
